canonical_data: local working trees, terminal state, agent conversations, plans, diffs, workflows, and optional Oz task state
current_repo_note: Most of the Warp repository is AGPL-3.0; the warpui_core and warpui UI framework packages are MIT. Optional Oz hosted runners and managed orchestration are separate cloud boundaries.
strengths: Terminal, editor, agent plans, diffs, review, and command execution share one mature local interface
Runs built-in and third-party CLI agents while adding approvals, notifications, and review tooling
Oz extends the same workflow to parallel local, self-hosted, or managed cloud agents
weaknesses: The combined terminal, editor, agent, and cloud-orchestration surface is broad and operationally complex
Hosted Oz work introduces a materially different data and execution boundary from local Warp
Agent shell access and unattended cloud tasks require careful approval, credential, and cost controls
why_it_matters: A large-scale attempt to make the terminal itself an open agentic development environment while supporting both native and competing command-line agents.
